sections.html: Cleveland County is in central Oklahoma, with Norman as county seat and the University of Oklahoma there. The April 2020 count was 295,514 residents, and the towns include Etowah, Lexington, Moore, Noble, Slaughterville and Norman. Housing here dates from several different eras depending on the town, so a Moore ranch house and a newer Norman subdivision home will not be assessed alike. Rentals and inherited houses are a common sale in a college county, and both come with their own tax paperwork.

Property tax is handled in the Norman courthouse, 201 S. Jones Ave. Both offices keep weekday hours from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., closed on holidays.

  • Assessor: Room 120, (405) 366-0230.
  • Treasurer: Suite 100, west side of the courthouse, (405) 366-0217.

Fair market value is decided by the Assessor each year, and a 12 percent assessment ratio applies to both real and personal property. Billing and collecting belong to the Treasurer, who also has a night drop box on the courthouse's north side. If a personal property warrant is overdue, you settle it at the Sheriff's Office, 111 N. Peters Ave., Suite 600.

Ask the Assessor why your value is what it is, and ask the Treasurer what you owe today.

sections.h2: Due dates and the tax calendar
sections.html:
Bills go out in the latter half of November, and you need a postmark or payment before January 1. When the tax tops $25.00 the Treasurer allows two installments: half ahead of January 1 and the remainder ahead of April 1. The first installment has to be at least exactly half.

Cleveland County tax calendar
DateEvent
January 1Assessment date for real and personal property
January 1 to March 15Listing period and exemption applications at the Assessor
April 1Board of Equalization begins adjusting the roll
May 31Board of Equalization adjourns
August 15Pay in full by this date to avoid publication of delinquent accounts
SeptemberDelinquent accounts are published
October 1Tax roll delivered to the Treasurer
Latter half of NovemberTax statements mailed

Interest and fees on unpaid taxes are not the Treasurer's to forgive. Relief, if any, has to come through the Assessor's protest process. You also cannot prepay taxes, with the exception of mobile homes on Form 936R.

sections.h2: Ways to pay and what they cost
sections.html:
Options include the counter, the mail, the drop box and the website. Only the website adds fees, and they go to the processor: 2.3 percent on credit cards, $3.95 on debit cards and $0.75 on electronic checks.

A mobile home paid on Form 936 must use cash, a cashier's check or a money order. Personal checks and credit cards do not work for it.

Homes with an escrow account are usually paid by the mortgage company, and many lenders send the money on the last day of the year. The county's records may take 5 to 7 days to show it. Ask your lender whether escrow has paid before you assume the balance is clear. The county's statement site is taxes.clevelandcountytreasurer.org, and after closing a new buyer can send an address change to CountyTreasurer@ClevelandCountyOK.com so statements arrive in their name. Keep a copy of the last statement paid, since title agents often ask to see it.

Homestead status takes $1,000 off assessed valuation. The county puts the saving at roughly $75 to $125, depending on location. Qualifying means Oklahoma residency, plus owning and living in the house on January 1, with the deed executed by that date and filed with the County Clerk by February 1.

  • Additional homestead: another $1,000 for a head-of-household owner whose gross household income last calendar year was $30,000 or less.
  • Senior valuation freeze: for a head of household 65 or older before January 1 who owns and occupies the home, with income at or below the HUD median level for the preceding year. There is no yearly reapplication.
  • 100% disabled veteran exemption: removes the full fair cash value of the homestead, on OTC Form 998 with VA documentation.
  • State credit or refund: Form 538-H for owners 65 or older or totally disabled with income of $12,000 or less.

Additional homestead and freeze applications run January 1 to March 15, or within 30 days of a valuation increase notice. Send them to applications@okco14.org or bring them to the Assessor's counter.

The Assessor is the first stop for any valuation complaint. Form 974, the state's informal protest, must be filed in writing within 30 calendar days of the date your valuation notice was mailed.

From April 1 to May 31 the Board of Equalization takes over, and the Assessor appears before it on disputes. Bring the evidence the form asks for: a recent sale of a similar house, an appraisal, photographs of defects or a corrected square footage.

If you lost an appeal, keep the paperwork for your buyer. Protest rights after closing belong to the buyer.

A short checklist keeps tax questions from slowing an offer. Print your parcel's tax statement from the county site, note which exemptions you hold, and write down what the escrow company has paid so far. If your home is a rental, ask the Treasurer whether any personal property tax is attached to the same name. A buyer's agent in Norman, Moore or Noble will ask these questions early, and a prepared seller answers them without a delay.

If you inherited the property, the tax statement may still list a relative's name. Fix that with the Assessor and the Treasurer before you list, because mail and notices go to the name on file, and an unopened valuation notice can cost you your protest window. Cleveland County mails notices to whoever the Assessor has on record, so keep that address current until the sale closes, and forward anything that arrives afterward to your title agent or the buyer.

sections.h2: Handling the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
Handle the tax balance as a line on the settlement statement, paid out of your proceeds. The county may lien real estate for a tax debt, and no buyer gets clear title until delinquent taxes are cleared.

  1. Get today's balance from the Treasurer or the online tax site.
  2. Find out if your mortgage escrow has paid, and allow 5 to 7 days for it to post.
  3. Make sure no personal property warrant is open under your name at the Sheriff's Office.
  4. Collect proof of each exemption, so the title company and buyer see a tidy record.
  5. After closing, send the Treasurer a change of address.

A vacant, inherited or rental house, or one behind on taxes, can sell for cash without repairs or showings. The same tax steps apply whoever the buyer is.

faqs.q: What is the Cleveland County tax deadline?
faqs.a: Payment or a postmark is needed before January 1. If the bill is over $25.00 you may pay half by then and the rest before April 1.

faqs.q: Where is the Cleveland County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: Suite 100 of the courthouse at 201 S. Jones Ave., Norman, OK 73069, on the west side. Call (405) 366-0217, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: What are the online payment fees for Cleveland County taxes?
faqs.a: The processor charges 2.3 percent on credit cards, $3.95 on debit cards and $0.75 on electronic checks. These are third-party fees, not county tax.

faqs.q: How much is the Cleveland County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It removes $1,000 of assessed valuation, worth about $75 to $125 depending on location. Ownership and residence on January 1 are required.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cleveland County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Clear title waits on the delinquent taxes, so the balance is normally paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
